title: Grateful Dead Live at Nassau Coliseum on 1973-09-08
source: Matrix 2 Source Mix - SBD (shnid=183) SBD> master reel> cassette> Dat >HD> shn; transfer by T. Wul + AUD (shn id 126070) source: aud cassette master; taped by Jim Cooper; sony ecm22p's > hitachi trq-222; nak dragon > benchmark adc1 24/96 > adobe audition cs6 16/44.1 > flac; transfer & seed - Rob Berger - matrix mixing by Kevin Tobin

ai_review.summary: A comforting matrix recording with prominent crowd ambience captures a beloved early‑1973 performance, highlighted by a warm Bertha intro.
ai_review.review: Both reviewers rave about the emotional power of this show, calling it their favorite Dead concert and praising the youthful, hungry playing of Jerry on his Strat. The matrix source blends audience sounds nicely—though occasional chatter can intrude—but adds to the nostalgic atmosphere, making the recording a pleasant listening experience despite its quirks.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is rated very high (comforting, standout early‑Dead energy) while recording quality is good but with noticeable crowd intrusion; weighted average yields ~4.3.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Audience mix is well integrated yet occasionally overwhelms the band (conversations, people shouting "rolling papers"); overall funky mixing but still clear enough to enjoy.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Reviewers describe the concert as having an exceptionally comforting flow that surpasses many classic shows, with a strong early‑Dead vibe and memorable transitions.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Pre‑Wall Strat work described as sharp, hungry, and highly enjoyable.
band_member_comments.Phil: Intro to Bertha features Phil's strong bass entry, noted as especially comforting.
